decision: reject D and current DWQ for release promotion
reason: D solves fewer tasks with more bytes and total generation time
DWQ worsens independent teacher validation loss and adds development truncations
Matched MXFP4 solves one more development task at smaller size
Heldout one-task gain is too small and takes 31.1% more generation time than MXFP4
Matched M4 synthetic decode is 14.8–16.8% lower than MXFP4 with more allocator memory; initial finite-smoke stage had critical pressure samples and material swap
next_action: One C DWQ repeat at learning rate 1e-7, same frozen corpus and uncalibrated/MXFP4 controls; test loss degradation without increasing weights
limitations: 24 familiar development tasks and 12 mixed synthetic heldout tasks, single greedy CUDA run, 4292 scored calibration tokens; no superiority proof or fresh repository evaluation
